grammarFocus: Expressing frequency: adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, hardly ever, never) before the main verb and after be; time expressions (twice a week, every night, once a term) at the beginning or end of the sentence
Present simple questions and short answers: do/does + subject + main verb; question word (what time, how often, where…) at the beginning; Yes, I do / No, I don't
Rules: must, mustn't, have to / has to, don't have to, can't, should; imperatives (Don't…, Never…)
Making suggestions, offering, agreeing and disagreeing: shall/could; how about / what about + -ing; maybe/perhaps; I'm afraid…

Thứ tự phương án R6–R25 được sắp để phân bố đáp án đều.
Email theo khung giáo viên: From/To/Date/Subject, It should be quite easy to…, First/Then/Next/After that/Finally, Don't forget to… when you've finished, Best wishes + chữ ký 3 dòng.

parts.instructions: Listen to the phone call and choose the best answer A, B, C or D (Questions L1–L5).
parts.context: Jack, the owner of a small dental clinic, phones Anna at SafeStore, an online backup company.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Good morning, SafeStore. Anna speaking. How can I help?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Hello. I run a small dental clinic, and I'm looking for an online backup company. Can I ask a few questions?

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Of course.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: First, how often do you back up the files?

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Our standard plan backs up your files every night at midnight. Our business plan does it every hour.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: I see. And where do you keep the data? Patient records are very private.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: All our servers are in two data centres in the UK. We never store data outside the country, and everything is encrypted.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Good. Do you charge for each computer?

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: No, we don't. We charge by the amount of storage you use. The standard plan costs twenty pounds a month for five hundred gigabytes.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: That should be enough for us. What happens if I lose a file? Do I call you?

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: You can, but most customers usually restore files themselves on our website. It only takes a few minutes.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: And does your helpline open at weekends?

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Yes, it's open every day, from seven in the morning until eleven at night.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Great. Could you send me some information by email?

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Certainly. What's your email address?

options.text: He wants to find an online backup company.
He wants to apply for a job.
He has lost some patient records.
He wants to buy new computers.

questions.explanation: Jack nói "I'm looking for an online backup company. Can I ask a few questions?". Việc mất tệp chỉ là câu hỏi giả định (What happens if I lose a file?).

questions.stem: How often does the business plan back up files?
questions.explanation: "Our business plan does it every hour." Mỗi đêm lúc nửa đêm là gói standard.

questions.stem: Where does SafeStore keep its customers' data?

options.text: In one data centre outside the UK
In two data centres in the UK

questions.explanation: Anna: "All our servers are in two data centres in the UK. We never store data outside the country".

questions.stem: How does SafeStore charge its customers?
questions.explanation: Jack hỏi có tính theo từng máy không; Anna trả lời "No, we don't. We charge by storage."

questions.stem: When is the SafeStore helpline open?

options.text: Every day, from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m.
Monday to Friday, from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m.

questions.explanation: "Yes, it's open every day, from seven in the morning until eleven at night."

parts.instructions: Listen to the message and answer the questions. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each answer (Questions L6–L10).
parts.context: Andrew from the IT department leaves a voice message for all staff about new security rules.

script.speaker: Andrew
script.text: Hello, everyone. This is Andrew from the IT department. I'm calling about the new IT security rules, which start on the first of April. Please listen carefully.

script.speaker: Andrew
script.text: First, updates. From April, the system installs security updates every Thursday at lunchtime, so you mustn't switch your computer off on Thursdays until three o'clock. The system always shows a warning ten minutes before it restarts.

script.speaker: Andrew
script.text: Second, USB sticks. You mustn't use your own USB sticks on company computers any more. If you need to move files, please use the shared drive instead.

script.speaker: Andrew
script.text: Third, laptops. When you take a laptop out of the office, you have to carry it in a locked bag, and you should never leave it alone in a café or on a train.

script.speaker: Andrew
script.text: Finally, we're running a short training session about the new rules on Wednesday the twenty-fifth of March at two o'clock in Room 4B. All staff have to attend, but it takes less than an hour. If you have any questions, call me on extension 418. Thanks very much.

questions.stem: On what date do the new rules start?
questions.explanation: "the new IT security rules, which start on the first of April".

questions.stem: On which day does the system install security updates?
questions.explanation: "the system installs security updates every Thursday at lunchtime".

questions.stem: How long before it restarts does the system show a warning?
questions.explanation: "The system always shows a warning ten minutes before it restarts."

questions.stem: What should staff use to move files instead of USB sticks?
questions.explanation: "If you need to move files, please use the shared drive instead."

questions.stem: In which room is the training session?
questions.explanation: "a short training session … at two o'clock in Room 4B".

matching.instructions: Match the terms (1–5) with the correct definitions (A–F). There is one extra definition that you do not need (Questions 1–5).

definitions.text: An official written record of what is said and decided at a meeting.
A large amount of data stored in a computer system so that you can find and use it easily.
A company or person that provides a service.
A copy of something that has been changed so that it is slightly different.
Someone who supervises the department of a company that people call for help, especially with computer problems.
To play sound or video on your computer while it is being downloaded from the Internet, rather than saving it as a file and then playing it.

items.explanation: Helpdesk supervisor (trưởng nhóm hỗ trợ kỹ thuật) quản lý bộ phận mà mọi người gọi đến khi cần giúp, nhất là sự cố máy tính.
Provider (nhà cung cấp dịch vụ) là công ty hoặc người cung cấp một dịch vụ. Định nghĩa B là của database (cơ sở dữ liệu), không có trong danh sách thuật ngữ.
Minutes (biên bản họp) là bản ghi chính thức những gì được nói và quyết định trong cuộc họp.
Stream (phát trực tuyến) là phát âm thanh, video trong khi đang tải từ Internet, không lưu thành tệp rồi mới phát.
Version (phiên bản) là một bản đã được thay đổi nên hơi khác bản trước.

grammar.stem: Our team backs up all the customer files ______.
grammar.explanation: Cụm thời gian chỉ tần suất: twice + a + week (hai lần một tuần), thường đứng cuối câu. Các phương án khác sai trật tự hoặc thiếu mạo từ.

grammar.stem: What time ______ the computer shop close on Saturdays?
grammar.explanation: Câu hỏi thì hiện tại đơn: từ để hỏi (What time) + does + chủ ngữ số ít (the computer shop) + động từ nguyên mẫu (close).

grammar.stem: 'Do you work at weekends?' '______ I only work from Monday to Friday.'
grammar.explanation: Câu hỏi bắt đầu bằng "Do you…?" thì trả lời ngắn "No, I don't." Không dùng "I'm not" (câu hỏi không dùng be) hay "I doesn't".

grammar.stem: Our receptionist ______ answer the phone until six o'clock every evening.
grammar.explanation: Nghĩa vụ trong công việc: chủ ngữ số ít (Our receptionist) dùng "has to". "must" không đi với "to"; "needs" phải là "needs to".

grammar.stem: You ______ take photos in the data centre. Cameras are not allowed.
grammar.explanation: "Cameras are not allowed" là điều cấm: "can't". "don't have to" chỉ nghĩa là không bắt buộc, không phải cấm.

grammar.stem: ______ email attachments from people you don't know. They may contain viruses.
grammar.explanation: Câu mệnh lệnh phủ định: Don't + động từ nguyên mẫu: "Don't open…".

grammar.stem: '______ I show you how the new printer works?' 'Yes, please. I've never used it before.'
grammar.explanation: Lời đề nghị làm giúp: "Shall I + động từ nguyên mẫu?", đáp lại "Yes, please". "Am I show", "Have I show" sai ngữ pháp; "Does" không đi với chủ ngữ "I".

vocabulary.stem: Before you can use this program, you need to ______ it on your computer.
vocabulary.explanation: Install (cài đặt) là thêm phần mềm vào máy tính để sẵn sàng sử dụng.

vocabulary.stem: The technician ran several tests to ______ the fault in the printer.
vocabulary.explanation: Diagnose (chẩn đoán) là tìm ra nguyên nhân của lỗi sau khi kiểm tra.

vocabulary.stem: Mai is ______ for the company website, so she decides what goes on it.
vocabulary.explanation: Be responsible for (chịu trách nhiệm về) cái gì: Mai phụ trách website nên quyết định nội dung.

vocabulary.stem: Our sales team uses a ______ with slides and pictures to show new products to clients.
vocabulary.explanation: Presentation (bài trình chiếu) là tài liệu do chương trình máy tính tạo ra để giới thiệu sản phẩm, ý tưởng mới hoặc hiển thị thông tin.

vocabulary.stem: Please keep all customer ______ on the company server, not on USB sticks.
vocabulary.explanation: Data (dữ liệu) là thông tin ở dạng có thể lưu và sử dụng trên máy tính.

vocabulary.stem: Kono Electronics is a large ______ of phones and TVs. It makes millions of them every year.
vocabulary.explanation: Manufacturer (nhà sản xuất) là công ty làm ra hàng hoá với số lượng lớn.

vocabulary.stem: Our office has a fast wireless ______, so all the computers and printers can share information.
vocabulary.explanation: Network (mạng) là một nhóm máy tính được nối với nhau để chia sẻ thông tin.

vocabulary.stem: I ______ my email three times a day: in the morning, after lunch and before I go home.
vocabulary.explanation: Check email (kiểm tra thư điện tử) là xem có nhận được thư mới không.

passage.title: Job Vacancy: IT Support Technician at Orbis Travel
paragraphs: Orbis Travel is one of the largest travel companies in Scotland. It sells holidays online and through twelve shops in Edinburgh, Glasgow and Aberdeen. The company's IT department has nine staff, and it is now looking for a full-time IT support technician to join the team at its head office in Glasgow.

The technician will look after the computers, phones and printers of the company's 150 employees. Most problems are simple, such as a forgotten password or a printer that will not work, and the technician usually solves them by phone or by connecting to the user's computer from the office. Once a week, the technician visits one of the shops to check the equipment and talk to the staff there.

Working hours are from 8.30 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. The technician also has to work one Saturday a month, when the shops are busiest, and gets a free day the following week. The job does not involve any travel outside Scotland.

Applicants must have at least one year's experience in a similar job, and they should be good at explaining technical problems in simple language. A driving licence is useful but not necessary, because all the shops are near train stations. The salary is £24,000 a year, and staff get a 20% discount on holidays. To apply, send your CV and a short letter to Fiona Reid, the IT manager, before 30th June.

questions.explanation: Đoạn 1: "It sells holidays online and through twelve shops".

options.text: By sending the computer to Glasgow
By phone or by connecting to the user's computer

questions.stem: What happens after the technician works on a Saturday?

options.text: They get twice the normal pay.
They visit a shop on Monday.
They get a free day the following week.

questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: kỹ thuật viên làm một thứ Bảy mỗi tháng "and gets a free day the following week".

questions.stem: What does the advertisement say about a driving licence?

options.text: It is useful but not necessary.
Only staff in Glasgow need one.

questions.explanation: Đoạn 4: "A driving licence is useful but not necessary, because all the shops are near train stations."

passage.title: The Hub Co-working Space: Questions and Answers
paragraphs: Who works at The Hub? Most of our members are freelance designers and developers, but we also have a few small companies with two or three staff.
When is The Hub open? We are open from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. every day, including weekends. Members with a Gold card can use The Hub twenty-four hours a day.
Do I have to book a desk? No, you don't. Just come in and choose a free desk. However, you have to book the meeting room at least one day before you need it.

How fast is the Wi-Fi? It is very fast, and our technician tests the connection every morning. Please don't connect more than two devices at the same time, because this slows down the network for everyone.
Can I print documents? Yes. Each member can print 100 pages a month free of charge. After that, each page costs 5p.
Can I bring my dog? I'm afraid not. Pets are not allowed in the building.

questions.explanation: Đoạn 1: "Most of our members are freelance designers and developers".

questions.statement: Members with a Gold card can use The Hub twenty-four hours a day.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: "Members with a Gold card can use The Hub twenty-four hours a day."

questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: "Do I have to book a desk? No, you don't." Chỉ phòng họp mới phải đặt trước một ngày.

questions.statement: The technician tests the Wi-Fi connection once a week.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 4: "our technician tests the connection every morning" (mỗi sáng), không phải mỗi tuần một lần.

questions.statement: Members can print as many pages as they want free of charge.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 5: mỗi thành viên chỉ được in miễn phí 100 trang một tháng; sau đó mỗi trang mất 5 xu.

email.task:
You are the office manager. Jenny is a new receptionist in your company. Write an email to Jenny explaining how to give a visitor access to the guest Wi-Fi, using the notes below. In your email you must use:
- at least two adverbs of frequency or time expressions (always, never, every Monday);
- at least two rule structures (must, mustn't, have to, should) or imperatives.
Follow the standard layout for an email giving instructions: From / To / Date / Subject, a greeting, It should be quite easy to …, the steps with First / Then / Next / After that / Finally, a reminder (Don't forget to … when you've finished.), then Best wishes and your name, position and department.
Write 80–100 words (do not count the From, To, Date and Subject lines).
bullets: ask the visitor to sign the visitors' book / always check their ID
give them a guest Wi-Fi card from the top drawer (the password changes every Monday)
never give visitors the staff Wi-Fi password
show them how to connect to the "Guest" network
if the connection doesn't work, call the helpdesk on extension 200
reminder: lock the drawer when you've finished
targetGrammar: Adverbs of frequency and time expressions (at least two): always, never, every Monday
Rules (at least two): must, mustn't, have to, should; imperatives (Ask…, Never give…)
email.modelAnswer:
From: Tran Bao Ngoc
To: Jenny
Date: 12th October
Subject: Guest Wi-Fi for visitors

Dear Jenny,

It should be quite easy to give visitors access to the guest Wi-Fi.
First, ask the visitor to sign the visitors' book. You must always check their ID.
Then, give them a guest Wi-Fi card from the top drawer. The password changes every Monday.
Next, show them how to connect to the "Guest" network. Never give visitors the staff password.
After that, just check that the connection works.
Finally, if it fails, call the helpdesk on extension 200.
Don't forget to lock the drawer when you've finished.

Best wishes,
Tran Bao Ngoc
Office Manager
Administration Department

parts.instructions: Answer the three questions. Speak for 30–45 seconds for each question.
questions: What do you usually do on a normal weekday? Talk about your routine. Use adverbs of frequency and time expressions (always, often, hardly ever, once a week, at the weekend).
Ask a classmate three questions about their part-time job or their university timetable. Use present simple questions (Do you…? How often do you…? What time does…?).
What rules does your family have about using phones or the internet at home? Use must, mustn't, have to, don't have to or can't.

parts.instructions: Describe someone's working week. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: Look at the weekly timetable of Tuan, a database administrator. Describe his duties and how often he does each one. Use the present simple and adverbs of frequency or time expressions (always, usually, every evening, twice a month, every Thursday), and say which task you think is the most important and why.
cues: every evening, 6.00: back up the customer database
Monday morning: check how fast the database answers queries
twice a month: update staff permissions
every Thursday, 2.00: meeting with the developers
never deletes old data without a backup
requiredGrammar: Present simple for duties: She checks…, She trains…
Adverbs of frequency and time expressions: always, usually, every day, twice a week, once a month, never
parts.sampleAnswer: Tuan is a database administrator, and his week is quite busy. Every evening at six o'clock, he backs up the customer database, so the company never loses its data. On Monday mornings, he usually checks how fast the database answers queries, because slow queries make the staff angry. Twice a month, he updates the staff permissions, for example when someone joins or leaves a team. Every Thursday at two o'clock, he has a meeting with the developers to talk about changes to the database. He never deletes old data without a backup. I think the most important task is the evening backup, because if the database crashes, the company can get all its information back.

parts.instructions: Deal with the situation. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: Your office prints too much paper, and printing costs are very high. In a meeting, respond to your colleagues' ideas in the cues, then make at least two suggestions of your own. Use shall or could, how about / what about + -ing, maybe or perhaps, and I'm afraid… to disagree politely.
cues: Colleague's idea 1: remove all the printers from the office → disagree politely and give a reason
Colleague's idea 2: print on both sides of the paper → agree
Your suggestions: set a monthly printing limit for each person / send documents by email / share files on the company server
requiredGrammar: Suggestions: Shall we…?, We could…, How about / What about + -ing?
parts.sampleAnswer: Thanks for your ideas. I'm afraid I don't agree with removing all the printers. Some of our clients still want paper contracts, and we sometimes need to print them quickly. But I agree that we should print on both sides of the paper. That's an easy way to save money. I also have some suggestions. How about setting a monthly printing limit for each person, for example two hundred pages? Maybe we could send more documents by email instead of printing them. And what about sharing meeting documents on the company server? Then everyone can read them on their laptops. Shall we try these ideas for three months and then check the costs again?
